{{Use shortened footnotes|date=May 2021}}
{{notability|date=June 2020}}

In mathematics, specifically in [[order theory]] and [[functional analysis]], a [[Filter on a set|filter]] <math>\mathcal{F}</math> in an [[order complete]] [[vector lattice]] <math>X</math> is '''order convergent''' if it contains an [[Order bounded set|order bounded]] subset (that is, a subset contained in an interval of the form <math>[a, b] := \{ x \in X : a \leq x \text{ and } x \leq b \}</math>) and if 
<math display=block>\sup \left\{ \inf S : S \in \operatorname{OBound}(X) \cap \mathcal{F} \right\} = \inf \left\{ \sup S : S \in \operatorname{OBound}(X) \cap \mathcal{F} \right\},</math> 
where <math>\operatorname{OBound}(X)</math> is the set of all order bounded subsets of ''X'', in which case this common value is called the '''order limit''' of <math>\mathcal{F}</math> in <math>X.</math>{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=234–242}} 

Order convergence plays an important role in the theory of [[vector lattice]]s because the definition of order convergence does not depend on any topology.

== Definition ==

A net <math>\left(x_{\alpha}\right)_{\alpha \in A}</math> in a [[vector lattice]] <math>X</math> is said to '''decrease to''' <math>x_0 \in X</math> if <math>\alpha \leq \beta</math> implies <math>x_{\beta} \leq x_{\alpha}</math> and <math>x_0 = inf \left\{ x_{\alpha} : \alpha \in A \right\}</math> in <math>X.</math> 
A net <math>\left(x_{\alpha}\right)_{\alpha \in A}</math> in a vector lattice <math>X</math> is said to '''order-converge''' to <math>x_0 \in X</math> if there is a net <math>\left(y_{\alpha}\right)_{\alpha \in A}</math> in <math>X</math> that decreases to <math>0</math> and satisfies <math>\left|x_{\alpha} - x_0\right| \leq y_{\alpha}</math> for all <math>\alpha \in A</math>.{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|p=8}} 

== Order continuity ==

A linear map <math>T : X \to Y</math> between vector lattices is said to be '''order continuous''' if whenever <math>\left(x_{\alpha}\right)_{\alpha \in A}</math> is a net in <math>X</math> that order-converges to <math>x_0</math> in <math>X,</math> then the net <math>\left(T\left(x_{\alpha}\right)\right)_{\alpha \in A}</math> order-converges to <math>T\left(x_0\right)</math> in <math>Y.</math> 
<math>T</math> is said to be sequentially order continuous if whenever <math>\left(x_n\right)_{n \in \N}</math> is a sequence in <math>X</math> that order-converges to <math>x_0</math> in <math>X,</math>then the sequence <math>\left(T\left(x_n\right)\right)_{n \in \N}</math> order-converges to <math>T\left(x_0\right)</math> in <math>Y.</math>{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|p=8}} 

== Related results ==

In an [[order complete]] [[vector lattice]] <math>X</math> whose order is [[Regular order (mathematics)|regular]], <math>X</math> is of [[Minimal vector lattice|minimal type]] if and only if every order convergent filter in <math>X</math> converges when <math>X</math> is endowed with the [[Order topology (functional analysis)|order topology]].{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}}
